chapter: Chick Webb, Lucky Roberts, Alex Jackson
title: The Savoy, Dixieland inspiration from the Memphis Five, Harry James
summary: Scott keeps his Sunday Dixieland band; says Harry James copied his style.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: And then the Savoy was nice, just opened, nice, nice, Of course, I left there before it got rough and rowdy. Still Sundays, I had that little band down at Ed Small's. See, those men -- we didn't need any music, they knew everything. And my inspiration had been from -- maybe -- there was a band out in Memphis called the Memphis Five. Years and years ago.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. They made records. Of course, I'm in New York, but I got their records. I like their style, Dixieland.

So I -- of course, I wasn't exactly stealing. But I liked the style they played. And I played that style down at Small's and they all went crazy about it. They went crazy about it. Strictly Dixieland. Yeah, because I'm not that type of player. Now, you know who stole from me? Harry James. He used to come up there and listen to me playing and all like that. I played on that style. Establish the tune and all like that, and then I'd improvise on my trumpet. As I felt, and that's the way he played.

But his father was a very rich man. And his father just put out money and got him a good agent, put him in, and the first thing you know, he's on Broadway. That money -- money talks. So he used to come up there. Yeah, Harry stole my stuff.
